subject: Acme - follow-up: feature parity & next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 15:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme discovery — feature parity & next steps

Hi Lisa — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary from our discovery:
- Primary goal: evaluate a low-latency, cost-predictable inference path for Acme's customer-facing assistant (multi-turn chat + tool calling).
- Key success metrics: median 95th-perc latency under 450ms for streaming token starts, correctness of function/tool calls for order lookup and billing inquiries, and structured JSON outputs for downstream processing.
- Current comparisons you mentioned: Hyperscaler managed endpoints (X Cloud), OpenAI API, and one self-hosted competitor.

Feature parity items we agreed to validate:
1) Function / tool calling: end-to-end correctness (schema enforcement + failure modes).
2) Structured outputs: deterministic JSON outputs for ingestion.
3) Streaming: token-level streaming performance and latency to first token.
4) Fallbacks & model variants: behavior when capacity or quota triggers fallback.

Proposed tests (we can run these or you can run with access we provide):
- Test A (function-calling correctness): run 200 synthetic calls with our sample order/billing prompts (attached test plan). Check % of correct schema vs total.
- Test B (streaming latency): 1,000 conversational turns distributed over 10 concurrent users to measure time-to-first-token and average token throughput.
- Test C (structured output ratio): evaluate forced-JSON outputs across 500 prompts and measure parsing success.

Next steps I suggest:
1) I'll share the test plan + a Redwood feature matrix showing behavior vs Hyperscaler/OpenAI (attached).
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive w/ your engineers — David (cc'd) to run through streaming config, function calling guarantees, and sample rollout strategy.
3) Agree on who will run tests (Redwood-run vs Acme-run) and share temporary creds or a shared repo.

If this looks right I can send calendar invites for the deep-dive and provision a test environment by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-devs@acme.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme discovery — feature parity & next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our internal notes. A few clarifications from our side and priorities: 

Priority items for Acme:
- Function/tool calling reliability is top priority (order/billing lookup must not hallucinate fields).
- Streaming start latency is next — our UX team measured user drop-off when first token > 500ms.
- Structured JSON outputs are required for our downstream pipeline; we need >98% parseable output.

We can run Test A and Test C on our side if you provide the sample prompts and expected schemas. For Test B (streaming), we'd prefer Redwood to run the initial 1,000-turn benchmark from a hosted test environment so we can compare apples-to-apples with your runtime.

Attached is a draft test plan (acme_test_plan.xlsx) and an internal doc with example schemas. I'll also add a short ticket in our shared repo with test data.

Two scheduling notes:
- Engineering availability for the deep-dive: Thu 19 Mar (10–12 PT) or Mon 23 Mar (14–17 PT).
- For procurement: procurement@acme.com may ask for a short FAQ on your data isolation and fallback policies — cc'ing them on the next thread.

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Chen | Head of Product Integrations, Acme Corp
lisa.chen@acme.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme discovery — feature parity & next steps

Thanks Lisa — adding a few technical commitments from our side so expectations are clear: 

What Redwood will provide for the tests:
- A pre-provisioned test environment running the same runtime and model variants we recommend for production (we'll mirror your concurrency and token limits).
- A Redwood-run streaming benchmark harness for Test B (we'll capture time-to-first-token and per-token throughput across regions).
- A function-calling correctness harness that validates schema outputs and collects failure cases for manual review.

What we need from Acme:
- A small set of production-similar prompts and example schemas (you mentioned you'd drop these in the shared repo).
- Confirmation on who will run Test A/C if you prefer internal runs (otherwise we can run both and share logs).

Operational notes:
- David can lead the deep-dive demo and will show how our continuous batching, KV caching, and streaming buffers affect latency. (David: can you prepare a short frag of the streaming demo and the function-calling edge-case results?)
- We'll prepare the Redwood feature matrix PDF comparing behavior vs X Cloud and OpenAI (see attached redwood_feature_matrix.pdf) and highlight known gaps.

I'll draft the calendar invite for Thu 19 Mar 10:30 PT and mark it tentative — Marissa, can you confirm?

— Neha
